plan_empty_body_member: The host has not built the plan yet. Once they do, you will see it here.

plan_hash_hint: The same input gives the same hash.
plan_day_empty: Nothing planned for this day yet.
plan_forbidden_body: The plan is visible to people on this trip. Ask the host.
plan_compute_failed: Could not build the plan. Try again in a moment.
plan_compute_forbidden: Could not build the plan. The host or a co-host builds it.
plan_total: Plan cost for the whole group: {amount}
people_empty_body_manage: Add people without an account, such as a child or a grandma. We set the values from their age.
people_empty_body_member: The host has not added anyone yet.
people_walk_value: {segment} km at a time, {daily} km a day
people_form_add_description: A name and an age are enough. We set the rest from the age.
people_form_edit_description: Change only what differs for this person.
people_form_defaults_hint: We set walking distance, activity and nap from the age. You can change them later.
people_form_segment_over_daily: A single walk cannot be longer than the daily distance.
people_error_has_account: This person has an account. Remove them under trip members, not here.
people_error_invalid: These values do not fit together. Check the distances and the nap.
people_form_stairs_hint: The higher the value, the less often the planner picks places with stairs. At a very high value such places are dropped entirely.
people_form_queue_hint: After how many minutes a queue is too long for this person.
people_form_floor_hint: The plan tries not to drop below this level, but at most to 60% of what the person would get alone. It has no effect with a single person.
people_roles_failed: Could not load the roles, so the list may not show the host and members with accounts.
trip_plan_body: The plan appears once the interview has collected everyone's preferences.
home_title: A trip where nobody feels they lost.
home_lede: A planner for family and group trips. Code does the maths; the language model only writes questions and explanations.
home_accounts_note: Kids and grandma do not need accounts: you add them as profiles and they vote through a link.
how_1_body: One sentence or a recording. The assistant only asks about what changes the plan most.
how_2_body: Want, don't mind or don't want, with a reason in one tap. Also through a link, no account needed.
how_3_body: Code, not the model, picks a plan where nobody drops below the floor. The same input gives the same plan.
proof_title: A chatbot plan sounds good until someone checks it.
proof_visible_body: A day plan with times, prices and a verdict. Tap a place to see who is for it and who is against.
proof_check_body: Paste a plan from any tool and TuttiTrip counts the problems: opening hours, distances, breaks, budget and accommodation requirements.
proof_price_body: Before the host overrides something, they see what it costs everyone else.
proof_settle_body: Code works out who pays whom, with the fewest transfers. An uncertain receipt reading is marked and needs your confirmation.
closing_title: Build a plan that works for everyone.
about_title: In a group, one person usually plans the whole trip.
about_lede: The child wants a theme park, the teenager something with friends, grandma a museum and a rest, and the partner something cheap and close. Chatbot plans sound good but ignore opening hours, distances and the pace of the slowest person.
about_split_1_body: Fairness solver, plan check, prices, accommodation requirements. No language model: the same input gives the same plan.
about_split_2_body: Interview questions, explanations, reading of pasted plans, offers and receipts.
about_split_3_body: Saving to your calendar, opening an accommodation search. It never buys or books anything on its own.
about_inside_plan_body: Every person rates places and code builds a plan where nobody drops below the floor.
about_inside_check_body: Counts the problems in a plan, including one that came from another tool.
about_inside_expenses_body: You log receipts and the settlement comes out with the fewest transfers.
about_team_body: Five people built this at HackYeah 2026 in Kraków, in the Artificial Intelligence category.
contact_lede: The HackYeah-TuttiTripTeam is on GitHub. That is where you find the project and us.
example_metric: lowest in the group, as a part of what the person could get alone
example_explainer: Each value is the part of what that person would get planning the trip alone.
